messages.author: 46f0fec04a5c6039
messages.subject: Feedback about the book/ggplot2
parts:
First for all I'd like to thank Hadley for implementing ggplot2 and so
graciously posting the draft of the book on-line: It really helped me
to understand the potential of the package. I would say that ggplot2
was a major factor for me in deciding to use R for most of my data
analysis needs: huge thanks!

I'd like to give some feedback about the book and ggplot2 based on
reading the Nov. 21 version.

Possible improvements:
1) add the R code used to generate each of the figures. Either in the
caption or in an appendix. For example I was trying to figure out to
draw the error bar + mean in page 77, Fig. 5.13 (left). I think is it
just stat_errorbar + geom_point, but I am not sure.
2) alpha is difficult to use since is bundled with deciding the color
scale. I would like to be able to modify any color scale with an alpha
option like coord_flip(), something like + scale_alpha(0.2) or
something to change all the point to transparent.
3) Some introduction to exploratory data analysis explaining best
practices by working through an example would be great.
4) More examples in the statistical summaries. The interaction of
summarization function and graphical elements is complex.
5) Chapter references would be more efficient if they gave the page
number as well as the chapter/section number.

Things that work great:

1) step by step examples really work for me: I loved 5.9 (annotating a
plot)
2) the pacing works pretty well from simple to complex
3) I really liked the toolbox chapter. would be nice to see more
additions there.
4) "Polishing your plots for publications" was also a great chapter.

Best regards,
Alex
